title: Console: 'Breadcrumb' Mode — minimal telemetry surface, scope reductions and acceptance matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Console shipping telemetry has grown beyond initial SLO and cost targets. For the upcoming limited launch window we need a pared-down runtime surface — internally called 'Breadcrumb' Mode — that preserves the most actionably diagnostic signals while trimming heavy cards, deep traces, and high-cardinality cost joins.

Goal: Define concrete scope reductions, acceptance criteria, and rollout gating for Breadcrumb Mode so PM/Design/Eng can deliver a safe, testable degraded experience that keeps teams operational during constrained capacity or when we intentionally limit cost exposure.

Success metrics: 1) Console end-to-end load p95 for a typical org view <= 500ms under synthetic load. 2) Observed telemetry ingestion cost delta <= -35% compared to current baseline on sampled workloads. 3) No more than 5% of user sessions hit missing-essential-data errors during a 5% canary rollout.

Why this differs from prior cuts: previous scope trims targeted feature parity across many cards. Breadcrumb Mode is an explicitly degradable product mode with a deterministic feature surface, documented fallbacks, and an operator-visible flag to flip between full and minimal surfaces.
scope_included: Dashboard: up to 6 prioritized cards with precomputed aggregates (latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost)
Tracing: aggregated service-level percentiles and 'open full trace' link (no full-span waterfall by default)
Cost breakdown: Top-5 routes by spend + 7-day delta; simplified currency formatting; no per-user breakdowns
Rollouts: feature-flagged Breadcrumb Mode (console.feature.breadcrumb) with 0/5/25/100 percent steps
Telemetry: event sampling and prefix caching metrics only (no raw token dumps)
scope_excluded: Live streaming of token-level cost or token-by-token trace streaming
High-cardinality joins in Cost Explorer (tags/labels group-by)
Per-route flamegraphs and full-span phased trace exploration in default view
Custom dashboard card creation for Breadcrumb Mode users
Long-retention raw trace storage surfaced in console (requires debug access)
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag exists and can be toggled at org and user levels via console.feature.breadcrumb
UI shows exactly the 6 prioritized cards for any org in Breadcrumb Mode; attempting to add cards shows a clear CTA to switch to Full Mode
Dashboard p95 load time <= 500ms for test orgs with 10k routes and 3k monthly requests in staging-sim under synthetic load
Tracing view surfaces aggregated latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95) and a single 'Open full trace in Debug Mode' button; clicking the button opens a gated debug overlay (auth enforced)
Cost explorer returns Top-5 routes and 7-day delta within 800ms for sampled orgs; aggregation correctness verified against ground-truth queries (<= 2% variance)
Telemetry ingestion volume from Breadcrumb Mode orgs is measured and shows >= 30% reduction in event count compared to Full Mode in a 24h A/B test

Canary rollout plan executed: 5% of orgs for 48h, monitor errors and key metrics; automated rollback triggers if session error-rate increases > 2x baseline OR customers experiencing missing-critical-data > 5%
Developer docs and operator runbook (feature flag, rollback, how to rehydrate full traces) published and linked from the console Admin page
End-to-end integration tests and synthetic performance harnesses added to CI that validate the minimal surface behavior
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal orgs only (engineering + SE) for smoke tests — 2 days
Canary: 5% orgs for 48 hours, automated monitor checks and manual ops review
Ramp: 25% orgs for 7 days if canary success criteria met
Full Launch: 100% optional opt-in for tenants; default for new tenants controlled by release flag in Q2
Fallback: operator flip to Full Mode with automatic rehydration path; rollback automation if thresholds exceeded
tradeoffs: Pro: reduces ingestion cost and UI latency, increases predictability under constrained capacity
Con: advanced debugging workflows temporarily harder for users; some customers will require opt-in to retain full visibility
Operational: rehydrating full traces for debugging will incur on-demand compute and storage spikes; need documented guardrails
Product: some product-led growth flows (deep trace share links) will be blocked in Breadcrumb Mode and require a conversion flow
risks: Customer confusion if Breadcrumb Mode enabled unexpectedly — mitigated by clear Admin messaging and banner in UI
Mis-calibrated aggregation could hide performance regressions — mitigate with shadow full-collection on 1% of requests for comparison
Rollout triggers false positives due to synthetic load mismatch — require real-org smoke checks and manual ops signoff
